World, Narrative and Irreverent Heroes

Status: Vision direction \| 22 November 2026

# Premise

The world prizes stories, prophecy, kingship, heroism, reputation, ancestry and the grand meaning of its crises. The playable protagonists are distracted, thrill-seeking, anti-story adventurers who don't accept that a quest's importance makes it compelling. They fixate on the coolest or most intriguing object, person, mechanism, challenge or forbidden door in the room. “We're all going to die anyway; might as well go out with a bang” captures their somewhat nihilistic appetite for epic experiences. They do not call themselves “Irreverents”; that is the game's title and a player-facing collective designation, NOT an in-world team name.

# The central comedic engine

1. An earnest authority or society assigns extraordinary meaning to a solemn situation.

2. The heroes notice a dozen more tempting opportunities within the same environment.

3. Player actions seize one opportunity: secretly, spectacularly, benevolently, maliciously, foolishly or inventively.

4. The world responds with serious material and social consequences.

5. Society tries to classify or reintegrate the heroes into its narrative; the heroes move on to the next curiosity.

Do not require a quip in every scene. The collision between a sincere world and unpredictable actions does the comedy.

# A genuinely important quest that nobody prioritizes

There is an overarching crisis—possibly an ancient evil, broken sacred seals, a royal prophecy or end of the world. The details of the antagonist, prophecy and outcome are NOT decided. It must matter to the world; the joke is not that the threat is fake. King, wizards, emissaries and villains repeatedly try to redirect the heroes toward it, while the heroes remain absorbed by treasure rooms, strange powers, secret routes, animals, armored champions and inadvisable stunts.

The main quest should be available but not design-protected as the only meaningful path. Do not funnel the party through mandatory boss gates to reach most content. When a major quest actor is undermined or attacked, favor consequence and continuity over “quest critical NPC” invulnerability, subject to practical scope.

# The heroes' motivation and individual flavors

The collective moral compass is “whatever seems most epic or interesting,” not a standard good/evil alignment. This permits a daring rescue, flawless nonviolent infiltration, outrageous theft, explosive destruction, suicidal stand, exploration of an impossible secret, or humiliation of authority. Individual hero personalities can value different kinds of epic: power/impact, stealth, discovery, risky stunts, tactical cleverness, extraordinary combat, creatures, machinery. These are brainstorming dimensions, not assigned final characters. Avoid a simplistic assumption they always pick violence.

# Townspeople oscillate between love and hate

The heroes can save a village and then rob it, repel the next threat and accidentally endanger everyone again. Towns, factions and NPCs may be grateful, infuriated, impressed, terrified, dependent and fascinated at once. Avoid a single morality meter that erases contradicting feelings. Social memory should matter to access, hospitality, suspicion, guard mobilization, prices, gifts, new opportunities, local reactions and ambient conversation. These are design targets, not fixed numeric attributes.

The heroes are “beloved catastrophes”: indispensable and intolerable, adored and feared, history-makers who never behave as history expects.

# Signature illustrative sequence: dragon, gift, jewels, arena

A party saves a town from a dragon and earns a gift: an invisibility cloak. They immediately use the cloak for a legendary theft of the town's prized jewels. The furious townspeople pursue them into an abandoned arena, which locks behind the crowd. The disturbance awakens hordes of undead gladiators. Now thieves and victims fight side by side for survival. The public oscillates from worship to betrayal to rage to renewed dependence. THIS IS A PLAYER-PROPOSED EXAMPLE OF THE DESIRED NARRATIVE QUALITY, not a confirmed required quest or exact NPC state chain.

An emergent version is preferable to a narrowly scripted one: dragon resolution, gifted ability, theft opportunities, pursuit, arena trap and undead encounter work as interacting world systems when feasible.

# The main quest's relationship to world time

The world can react to delays, shifting factions and worsening concern; do not force a countdown that invalidates the sandbox. The question of whether the central crisis advances without the player is OPEN. The first experience should communicate the freedom to ignore urgent narrative pressure.

# The villains and institutions

The king and royal court take apocalyptic stakes seriously. A villain may be outraged not because the heroes are winning but because they are not paying attention. Institutions should make plans, mobilize guards and tell stories about heroes that conflict with what actually happened. The world can learn to bait their attention by advertising an impossible feat, forbidden vault or unbeatable champion. These are strong tonal opportunities, not named-cast commitments.

# Story delivery

Prefer playable situations, environmental storytelling, conversations during movement, reactive NPC remarks, legends, rumors, and persistent consequences. Avoid lengthy forced cinematics that dictate moral interpretation or demand commitment to the designated main quest. Critically, the opening king's speech is deliberately long, but remains freely interruptible by gameplay.

# Moral and tonal guardrails

The game welcomes fictional anti-social mayhem and cartoonish overkill as forms of play, but consequences remain visible: anger, pursuit, destruction, fear, rebuilding, alliances and unexpected rescue. “Not moralizing” does not mean “NPCs don't care.” The exact content rating and visual treatment of defeated NPCs are OPEN. The world is whimsical in appearance but sincere in how its inhabitants experience danger and betrayal.

# What not to lock yet

No decided protagonist names, kingdom names, lore chronology, prophecy details, canonical moral ending, guaranteed princess death, required thief/dragon incident, or specific faction roster. Dialogue sketches are examples. The story should not become so prescriptive that it contradicts the game's anti-story premise.

PRIMARY WORLD PREMISE REFINEMENT — OWNER CONFIRMED 22 NOV 2026

Beyond caring about stories, the culture treats the HERO'S JOURNEY AS SACRED. Everyone wants their life and everything in the kingdom to fit the EXPECTED GLORIOUS MAIN QUEST PRECISELY. All characters are extremely typecast; objects and places have rigid, culturally accepted functions; everything is invested with tremendous meaning. The society's complete predictability is the dramatic foil for the heroes' unplanned, irreverent, concrete use of the same world.

A king is meant to issue a solemn quest; a sword is meant to defeat the designated villain; the royal champion is meant to fight honorably; a sacred key is meant to open its named door. The protagonists find other uses. Culture is rigid, but player-facing object/world systems should remain permissive. When the heroes break a pattern, ordinary people are horrified rather than immediately “welcoming” it as a new heroic chapter.

Full detailed direction: https://docs.google.com/document/d/16hzOOStE4Nt-uOcD6ApTDbWPT10fgizTC3eOcDB8Vmw/edit

OWNER TONAL CORRECTION — DELIGHTED ARCHETYPES (22 NOV 2026)

The world's inhabitants are not resentful prisoners of the sacred story. They are almost absurdly DELIGHTED to perform their roles. The shopkeeper loves being a shopkeeper, the blacksmith loves smithing the legendary sword, the sage delights in delivering cryptic guidance, and the villain may adore the magnificence of his villainy. Everyone is proud to take their proper part in the grand main quest, so the culture is genuinely happy, enthusiastic and intensely predictable. The protagonists' attention and creative misuse of things perplex or outrage people who have NO desire to escape their roles. Don't default to cynical or “oppressed and awaiting liberation” writing. Details: https://docs.google.com/document/d/16hzOOStE4Nt-uOcD6ApTDbWPT10fgizTC3eOcDB8Vmw/edit

LATEST NARRATIVE MECHANIC — OWNER CONFIRMED 22 NOV 2026

The intensely role-satisfied society is ABSOLUTELY HORRIFIED when the heroes fail to do the obvious thing. That shock drives wildly escalating resistance. But the instant heroes visibly resume proper role-conforming action, the same people settle quickly and happily declare everything is exactly as expected: “Yup! Just as expected!” This is a crucial tone and systems distinction: the world loves its script, recoils from improvisation, and rapidly trusts its script again. Full system elaboration: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1jQssgW8w1oXo_14lLhbGHVwWTPef7y2TEU_aCD_nMvQ/edit

CHARACTER ETHOS — D&D HOMAGE (OWNER DIRECTION, 22 NOV 2026)

The owner characterizes Irreverents as an homage to CHAOTIC NEUTRAL and the RULE OF COOL. This sharpens the protagonists' identity: they chase fascinating, epic possibilities rather than the prescribed good-guy storyline. They are not required to act villainous, antiheroic or destructive; the greatest epic moment might be a flawless, undetected infiltration, a sincere rescue, an impossible skillful stunt or an absurdly violent wrestling move. The game should support “Wouldn't it be awesome if…?” experiments with consistent consequences and memorable failure as well as success.

The world remains blissfully typecast. Villains adore properly villainous plots as much as merchants adore commerce; both can be narratively rigid and socially comfortable in an expected conflict. The player heroes, in contrast, are unpredictable because curiosity outranks the world's assigned meaning.

OWNER TONE REFINEMENT — THE WORLD PREMISE MOSTLY STAYS QUIET (22 NOV 2026)

The world still has a near-religious Hero's Journey culture and delighted typecasts, but the game should be predominantly low-dialogue like Kirby and LEGO Star Wars. Do not constantly turn that premise into exposition, punchlines, named religion-themed stages or NPC speeches. Let animation, behavior, sound and rare concise reactions reveal the contrast when players actually break expectations. Players should enjoy ordinary excellent platforming, secrets, powers, stealth and puzzles even when the joke is not present at all. This replaces over-lore-heavy level pitches as the correct tone.
